text:
Matias Maccelli has played only eight games for the Islanders, after injury kept him out, and they've been interesting ones. He's on the ice for 82% of the team's power-play time, up from 31% last season in Toronto, and he has six points.

That's the breakout case, and it's built on role, not luck: ice time settles faster than scoring does. But eight games is a small sample, and his scoring rate (3.11 points per 60) is above anything in our range for him. The Islanders have also scored 3.5 more goals than expected with him on.

What he brings is passing. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 20% of his setups coming across the royal road last season, against 7% for a typical forward, the pass that moves a goalie side to side. With Mathew Barzal and Ryan Pulock also back from injury, his job is to feed people. Our range: 33 to 54 points.
